items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: Well Hawkins, like Duke, like Louis, a creator.

ctx.x: Did he play violin with Mamey Smith? I don't think he did. I had an idea. Yeah, yeah.

Well Hawkins, like Duke, like Louis, a creator. And I always say that the imitators never, never greatest creators. To me Hawkins would always be the number one man. To me. A lot of those would come over and play a lot. A lot of those might blow Louis up. I mean Louis is still the king of that style. He's the creator. Hawkins was the creator of that fine saxophone player. A lot of them got a lot of good ones. But to me Hawkins has always number one. Always will be with Mamey.

In a sense I think that those clarinet players, Barney and Noon especially, were part of a family. In other words they were not especially creators even though they had great originality and you identify them immediately. They're of a family, maybe comes back from Teal. Teal and Bache.
